method: Blind: rater saw only X/Y text and the claim, not pairs_key.json, until all 25 were rated.
criterion: Which of X/Y better grounds a debater on THIS claim as a node reference inside a debate prompt: specific/concrete and on-topic for the claim beats generic taxonomic scope-setting (Encompasses/Excludes framing reads as documentation, not a usable debate reference).

ratings.why: directly engages the claim's displacement/workload framing; Y is scope-setting prose
takes a position on the claim's stat rather than listing what the node covers
mirrors the claim's own argument structure (concedes history, argues velocity is different)
names concrete governance precedent matching 'collective action, democratic oversight'; Y's scope is broader than the claim
directly addresses taxing AI profits, the claim's actual proposal
names the specific mechanism ('audit washing') the claim is defending against a characterization of
states the scope (statistical tracking of layoffs) that the claim's cited figure falls under; Y's rhetorical question is vaguer
mirrors the claim's rebuttal structure against the same accelerationist framing
names the specific mechanism (occupational segregation, exposure differential) behind the claim's stat
gives a concrete, checkable figure (300% undercount) matching the claim's concrete framing
directly argues the liability-extension point the claim is making
diagnoses intent, matching the claim's own diagnosis; Y proposes a remedy the claim doesn't ask for
states the market-failure rationale the claim is invoking for domain-specific liability
names the moral-hazard mechanism the claim's 'false economy' language is pointing at
the only one of the two naming developer-level pre-deployment accountability, which is what the claim is actually contrasting against deployer-level ATCB monitoring
echoes the claim's 'enforcement with teeth' framing directly
names the specific mechanism (pre-release impact assessments, continuous monitoring) the claim's 'enhanced pre-deployment review' is referring to
the richer mechanism list (falsifiable triggers, anti-gaming, escrow) covers the claim's 'performance-gated audits' more fully than Y's one example

the Excludes clause usefully distinguishes this from adjacent proposals, which matters since the claim's own mechanism (compute-hours tax) sits awkwardly between the fund and the excluded alternatives
near-paraphrase of the claim itself in argument form, directly usable as a debate line
directly engages the claim's 'adaptive safety integration... real-time' framing; X is jargon-heavy ('switchable infrastructure', 'off-meter') and harder to use as spoken grounding
closely mirrors the claim's Telemetry Compliance Board proposal
the Agile/iteration analogy matches the claim's 'two adaptive iterations' language directly
directly addresses 'machine speed, not committee speed' via oversight-panel scaling without bottlenecks
near-direct restatement of the claim's regulatory-capture argument
